scope.included: Rules, definitions, procedures, mechanical limits, tables, and campaign subsystems present in the uploaded document.
scope.omitted: Flavor text, examples, and non-mechanical exposition.
scope.note: The Strongholds and Domains section in this document is explicitly excerpted and replaced elsewhere; only the remaining domain rules present here are summarized.

definition.text: Campaign-scale magical work including spell research, item creation, ritual learning and casting, construct design and creation, crossbreeding, necromancy, and related projects.

eligibility.rule: Spellcasters of levels 0-4 may only assist higher-level casters.
At 5th level, a spellcaster may independently research spells, scribe scrolls, and brew potions.
At 9th level, a spellcaster may create more powerful magic items such as weapons, rings, and staffs.
At 11th level, a spellcaster may learn and cast ritual spells and craft magical constructs.
Chaotic spellcasters of 11th level or higher may create necromantic servants and may transform themselves into undead.

notes.note: Levels marked with * may only assist higher-level casters.

procedure.step: Roll a magic research throw.
Compare the result to the target value listed for the spellcaster's level, modified by project-specific adjustments.
Add the spellcaster's Intelligence bonus to the die roll.
If the spellcaster has the Magical Engineering proficiency, add proficiency rank to the roll.
An unmodified die roll of 1-3 always fails.
procedure.result: Success occurs if the modified result equals or exceeds the target value.
procedure.failure: On failure, all time and money spent are lost, and any precious materials or special components used are consumed.

eligibility.rule: A spellcaster must be 5th level or higher to independently research spells.
An arcane caster may research a spell only if he can still learn spells of that level.
A divine caster may research a spell only with the permission of his deity.
A deity will usually remove a spell of the same level from a divine caster's spell list in exchange for granting the new spell.

procedure.step: Choose a spell not otherwise available from scrolls, spell books, or deity.
Pay 1,000gp per spell level.
Spend 2 weeks per spell level in research.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: The target value is increased by 1/2 the spell's level, rounded down.
procedure.failure: Time, money, precious materials, and special components are lost.

procedure.step: Describe the intended spell and its effects in detail.
The Judge determines whether the spell can be created and, if so, its spell level.
The spellcaster must be capable of casting spells of that level.
Pay and spend time as for spell research unless otherwise ruled.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: For a new spell, increase the target value by the full spell level instead of half the spell level.

procedure.step: Spend 1,000gp and 2 weeks researching the item.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.result: On success, the item's properties are identified.
procedure.note: Potions and common magic items may instead be quickly identified using Alchemy and Magical Engineering, as referenced by the document.

definition.text: A required research resource for spell research and ritual learning.

subsection.rule: A spellcaster must have access to a library to research a spell.
A personal library requires a minimum investment of 4,000gp to allow research on 1st-level spells.
Each additional spell level that may be researched requires another 2,000gp of library investment.
For every 10,000gp of value above the minimum required for the spell level, the spellcaster gains +1 on the magic research throw, to a maximum of +3.
Each time a wizard successfully researches a spell, add 10% of the gold spent for that effect to the library's value.
Rare or authoritative tomes found as treasure may provide additional bonuses to research specific spells or categories of spells.

eligibility.rule: At 5th level, a spellcaster may create scrolls and potions.
At 9th level, a spellcaster may create other magic items such as rods, rings, swords, and other items.
An arcane spellcaster may never create magic items exclusive to divine spellcasters.
A divine spellcaster may create any item his class is eligible to use.

requirements.rule: To create a magic item, the spellcaster must know the spell or spells that replicate the item's effect, or possess a sample or formula of the item.
If the item's effect does not correspond to an existing spell, the spellcaster must either research a new spell producing the effect or obtain a sample or formula.
Special components are required for each spell effect.

procedure.step: Determine the item's effect category and base cost/time from the magic item creation table.
Confirm spell knowledge, formula, or sample availability.
Secure a workshop sufficient for the highest spell level or item bonus involved.
Acquire required special components.
Optionally add precious materials.
Spend the required cost and time.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: The target value is increased by the spell level being enchanted into the item.
If multiple effects are enchanted, roll separately for each effect.
procedure.equivalence: A +1 item bonus counts as a 1st-level spell effect.
A +2 item bonus counts as a single 3rd-level spell effect.
A +3 item bonus counts as a single 6th-level spell effect.

definition.text: A magical recipe for item creation.
An existing magic item available to the spellcaster while working.

subsection.rule: A spellcaster automatically has a formula for any magic item he has previously created.
Formulas may be found as treasure.

advantages.advantage: Allows creation without knowing or inventing the item's spell effects.
Reduces the target-value increase to 1/2 the level of the spell being imbued, instead of the full level.

subsection.rule: For every 10,000gp of gems, jewelry, precious metals, rare woods, or elaborately carved woods added to the project, the spellcaster gains +1 on the magic research throw.
A character may not spend more on precious materials than the base cost of the item.
Each spell effect in a magic item requires special components.
Components are usually organs or blood from monsters with total XP value equal to the gp cost of the research.
Component cost is in addition to the base cost of the research.
If the character lacks a formula when creation begins, he does not learn the required special components until the work is 50% complete.
The Judge determines the specific components required.
Different formulas for the same item may require different components.
A spellcaster must have access to a workshop to create magic items.
A personal workshop requires a minimum investment of 4,000gp to allow creation of 1st-level spell effects or item bonuses.
Each additional spell level or bonus requires another 2,000gp of workshop investment.
For every 10,000gp of value above the minimum required for the relevant spell level or bonus, the spellcaster gains +1 on the magic research throw, to a maximum of +3.

row.cell: 2 days x spell level x charges

notes.note: *If a charged item has multiple spell effects powered by the same charges, use the base cost and time for the highest-level spell effect, plus half the base cost and time for each additional spell effect. The minimum time to create a charged item is never less than 1 week per spell level of the highest-level effect.
**If the weapon or armor has a bonus restricted to a particular class or type of opponents, the extra bonus is half price.
**If the weapon or armor is enchanted with spell-like effects, those effects are enchanted separately using the cost and time for charged or permanent effects.
***Arrows, bolts, and slingstones are enchanted in bundles of 20 at a base cost of 10gp.

definition.text: A subordinate arcane helper who may perform additional magic item creation tasks under supervision.

subsection.rule: An assistant must be a mage or other arcane spellcaster of at least 1st level employed by an arcane spellcaster of 9th level or higher.
A 0th-level character with two ranks in Alchemy may function as an assistant in potion creation.
A spellcaster of 9th level or higher may supervise one assistant, plus one additional assistant per point of Intelligence bonus.
Whenever the supervising spellcaster works on item creation, each assistant may be assigned one additional magic item creation task.
An assistant must have a formula or sample to work from.
The assistant's success chance is based on the assistant's own level.

table.title: Sample Magic Item Time, Cost, and Components

eligibility.rule: Arcane and divine spellcasters of 11th level or higher may learn ritual spells.
Arcane ritual spells are 7th-, 8th-, and 9th-level arcane spells.
Divine ritual spells are 6th- and 7th-level divine spells.
Each ritual spell must be learned separately.
A spellcaster may know a number of rituals of each spell level equal to his prime requisite ability-score bonus (Intelligence for arcane, Wisdom for divine).

procedure.step: Spend 1,000gp per spell level.
Spend 2 weeks per spell level researching.
Use a library.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: Increase the target value by the full level of the ritual being researched.

procedure.step: Spend 500gp per spell level.
Spend 1 week per spell level casting.
Use a workshop.
Provide required special components.
Optionally provide precious materials for a bonus.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: Increase the target value by the full level of the ritual being cast.
procedure.rule: The special components required are learned when the ritual is learned.
procedure.option: The caster may have the ritual take effect immediately.
The caster may store the ritual effect on a scroll or as a charge in a ring.
procedure.rule: Storing the effect adds no extra cost; it is treated as creating a single-charge magic item with that spell effect.

ritual.effect: Increase the domain's Land Value by 2gp per peasant family for 12 months.

reverse_spell.name: Ravage
reverse_spell.effect: Decrease the domain's Land Value by 2gp per peasant family for 12 months.

ending_conditions.condition: Can be undone by remove curse cast by a spellcaster of equal or greater level.

ritual.effect: Functions like restore life and limb, except the subject is immediately restored to full hit points, vigor, and health with no side effects or lingering exhaustion.
ritual.rule: The condition of the remains does not matter.
Any small portion of the creature's body is sufficient.
The creature may have been dead no longer than 10 years per caster level.

reverse_spell.name: Destruction
reverse_spell.effect: The touched victim dies immediately and falls to dust.

ritual.effect: Create an ethereal passage through wood, plaster, or stone, but not through other materials.
ritual.rule: The passage is 10 feet deep and 5 feet in diameter.
The phase door is invisible and inaccessible to all creatures except the caster.
Only the caster may use the passage.
The caster disappears when entering and reappears when exiting.
The caster may take one other human-sized or smaller creature through the door; this uses two passages.
The passage does not permit light, sound, or spell effects through it and cannot be seen through.
The phase door is subject to dispel magic.
If dispelled while a creature is inside, the creature is harmlessly ejected as with passwall.

ritual.effect: Make another lower-level arcane spell effect permanent on a creature, item, or area.

limitations.rule: Cannot make permanent a spell that already has duration instantaneous or permanent.
Divine spells may only be made permanent with the deity's permission.
The Judge may forbid use with other specific spells for game-balance reasons.

target_limits.rule: An area may receive any number of permanency spells.
An item may receive up to five permanency spells.
After the first permanency on an item, each additional permanency carries a cumulative 20% chance of failure.
If item permanency fails, the item is destroyed completely.
A creature may receive one permanency without risk.
If a creature receives additional permanencies, it suffers side effects determined on the Tampering with Mortality table.

ending_conditions.condition: It lasts until dispelled by the caster or a higher-level spellcaster.
When dispelled, the bound spell effect vanishes immediately.

ritual.distinction: Binding a spell to an item with permanency is not the same as creating a true magic item; true magic items cannot be dispelled.

ritual.effect: Allows the caster to alter reality and duplicate the effects of any other spell or create comparable effects.

examples_of_permitted_scope.item: Bring the dead back to life.
Teleport a group to any location without error.
Grant unique powers or ability bonuses at the Judge's discretion.

limitations.rule: Wishes are fulfilled according to the letter of the request.
The Judge regulates scope and final limits.
Hostile wishes may be fulfilled in a technically valid but indirect manner.

eligibility.rule: Arcane and divine spellcasters of 11th level or higher may create and design constructs.
Dwarven craftpriests may create and design constructs starting at 9th level.

procedure.step: Choose or obtain a formula or sample of the construct type.
Determine Hit Dice and special abilities.
Pay 2,000gp per Hit Die plus 5,000gp per special ability.
Spend 1 week plus 1 day per 1,000gp of cost.
Maintain access to a workshop worth at least the cost of the construct throughout creation.
Optionally use precious materials for a bonus.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: Increase the target value by +1 per 5,000gp of construct cost.
procedure.rule: The spellcaster may only create constructs with HD no greater than twice his class level.
The remains of a destroyed construct may serve as a sample.
procedure.workshop_bonus: For every 10,000gp of workshop value above the minimum required, gain +1 on the magic research throw.

procedure.step: Determine the new construct's Hit Dice, Armor Class, attacks, maximum damage, and special abilities within the design limits.
Pay 2,000gp per Hit Die plus 5,000gp per special ability.
Spend 1 week plus 1 day per 1,000gp of cost.
Maintain access to a library worth at least the cost of the construct throughout design.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: Increase the target value by +1 per 5,000gp of construct cost.
procedure.success: A successful design creates a formula that can later be used to create the construct.
procedure.rule: The spellcaster may only design constructs with HD no greater than twice his class level.
procedure.library_bonus: For every 10,000gp of library value above the minimum required, gain +1 on the magic research throw.

design_rules.rule: Constructs must have at least 1 HD.
Default Armor Class equals 1/2 the construct's Hit Dice.
Most constructs are immune to poison, gas, charm, hold, and sleep; these together count as one special ability.
Each additional immunity counts as one additional special ability.
A construct may have 1 to 4 attacks per round.
Total maximum damage per round may not exceed three times the construct's HD.
Damage may be divided among attacks as desired.
Any special attacks or powers count as special abilities.

eligibility.rule: Arcane spellcasters of 11th level or higher may create crossbreeds.

progenitor_limits.rule: Each progenitor creature must have HD no greater than the creator's class level.
Each progenitor may not have more than one special ability, plus one additional special ability per point of the creator's Intelligence bonus.

design_rules.rule: The creator chooses the crossbreed's form before creation begins.

alignment.rule: If either progenitor is Chaotic, the crossbreed is Chaotic.
If both progenitors are Lawful, the crossbreed is Lawful.

movement.rule: The crossbreed may receive the movement capabilities of either progenitor or both.
Having both sets of movement counts as a special ability.

armor_class.rule: If the crossbreed uses one progenitor's movement, it has that progenitor's AC.
If it uses both movement modes, it takes the better AC.

hit_dice.rule: The crossbreed may have either progenitor's HD or any amount between them.

attacks.rule: The crossbreed may receive the attacks of either progenitor or both.
Having attacks from both progenitors counts as a special ability.
If the crossbreed has more HD than the progenitor from which its attacks are drawn, attack damage scales upward proportionally to the HD increase.

morale.rule: The crossbreed uses the better morale of the two progenitors.

special_abilities.rule: The crossbreed may have the special abilities of one, both, or neither progenitor.
Each special ability increases cost and difficulty.

type.rule: Depending on progenitors, they may also count as beastmen, enchanted creatures, giant humanoids, humanoids, oozes, or vermin, at Judge's discretion.
Crossbreeds may reproduce with others of their breed.
If they closely resemble one progenitor, they may also breed with that progenitor.

procedure.step: Choose progenitors and assign final traits within the design rules.
Pay 2,000gp per Hit Die of the finished crossbreed plus 5,000gp per special ability.
Spend 1 week plus 1 day per 1,000gp of cost.
Provide the progenitor creatures; they are killed during the process.
Maintain access to a special crossbreeding laboratory worth at least the cost of the crossbreed.
Optionally use precious materials for a bonus.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: Increase the target value by +1 per 5,000gp of crossbreeding cost.
procedure.rule: No special components are required beyond the progenitors.
procedure.laboratory_bonus: For every 10,000gp of laboratory value above the minimum required, gain +1 on the magic research throw.

control_rules.rule: A newly created crossbreed is not automatically under the caster's control.
If the more intelligent progenitor was intelligent and willingly participated, the crossbreed retains that progenitor's relationship to the caster.
Otherwise, the Judge makes a reaction roll to determine the crossbreed's reaction.

eligibility.rule: Chaotic spellcasters of 11th level or higher may transform creatures into intelligent undead.

limits.rule: The undead created may not have HD greater than the spellcaster's class level.
The undead may not have more than one special ability plus one additional special ability per point of the spellcaster's Intelligence bonus.

procedure.step: Choose a dead subject creature.
Ensure the creature has been dead no longer than 1 day per HD.
Pay 2,000gp per Hit Die plus 5,000gp per special ability.
Spend 1 day per 1,000gp of cost.
Maintain access to a private mortuary and embalming chamber worth at least the cost of the necromancy.
Provide required special components.
Optionally use precious materials for a bonus.
Make a magic research throw.
procedure.modifier: If the creature is willing, increase target value by +1 per 5,000gp of necromancy cost.
If the creature is unwilling, increase target value by +2 per 5,000gp of necromancy cost.
procedure.rule: The subject must be dead when the ritual is completed.
The success or failure is not known until the creature is dead.
A spellcaster may transform himself by killing himself at the conclusion of the ritual.
procedure.facility_bonus: For every 10,000gp of mortuary value above the minimum required, gain +1 on the magic research throw.

special_components.rule: Necromancy requires special components, usually organs or blood from monsters with total XP value equal to the cost of the research.
If the undead will have special abilities, the component creature must have at least as many special abilities.
If the undead requires special items such as a phylactery or coffin, these must be provided.
If the character does not know the components at the start, he learns them when the necromancy is 50% complete.
The Judge determines the specific components.

control_rules.rule: An undead created by necromancy is not automatically under the caster's control.
If the subject was a willing participant, it retains its prior relationship to the caster after becoming undead.
Otherwise, the Judge makes a reaction roll to determine its reaction.

definition.text: Ephemeral gp-equivalent spiritual power that divine spellcasters may apply to certain magical research projects.

uses.use: The gp value of divine power may substitute for some or all special components required to create a magic item or perform a ritual spell.
The gp value of divine power may substitute for an equivalent value of precious materials used to create a magic item, perform a ritual spell, create a construct, or grant undeath.

limitations.rule: Divine power may only be applied to projects that further the goals of the caster's patron deity.
It is accumulated only while actively working on an eligible magical research project.
Any unspent divine power remaining when the project ends is lost.

subsection.rule: Lawful divine spellcasters gain divine power by building congregations.
Every 50 congregants generate 10gp worth of divine power per week of faithful worship.

qualification.rule: Congregants must share the caster's alignment.
Congregants must worship the caster's deity.
Congregants must regard the caster as their spiritual advisor.

sources_of_congregants.rule: Party members, henchmen, and followers may form the core of a congregation.
Additional congregants may be recruited through charitable deeds, missionaries, and temple construction.

procedure.step: Each month, total the gp value of all charitable spells cast for peasants by the caster, henchmen, and followers, using spell-market prices from the referenced table.
Add the gp value of hirelings deployed as missionaries.
Add the gp value of religious structures erected in the realm.
For each full 1,000gp of proselytizing value, gain 1d10 plus Charisma bonus congregants.
procedure.limit: The caster cannot gain more congregants than exist in the realm being proselytized.

maintenance.rule: The monthly cost to maintain a congregation is 1gp per congregant.
If the maintenance cost is not paid, the caster loses 1d10 congregants per 1,000.
On a roll of 10, roll again and add the result; continue if more 10s are rolled.

domain_sources.rule: A divine spellcaster may also gain congregants by ruling a domain or serving as spiritual advisor to a ruler.
A ruler can command subjects to worship his god, but actual faith depends on domain morale.
The amount of divine power available from domain worship is listed on the Domain Worship table.
To become a ruler's spiritual advisor, the divine spellcaster generally must be the highest-level divine spellcaster with whom the ruler has Friendly relations.

columns.column: Divine Power per 10 Families per Week

subsection.rule: Chaotic divine spellcasters may also gain divine power through blood sacrifice.
A spellcaster may conduct no more than one blood sacrifice per class level per day.
A blood sacrifice must be performed in a chaotic temple, graveyard, or sinkhole of evil.
Each blood sacrifice takes one turn and requires a magic research throw.
If successful, the caster gains divine power equal to the XP value of the sacrificed creature.
Sacrificing an unwilling chaotic creature yields no divine power.
Sacrificing a willing chaotic creature does yield divine power.

procedure.step: When magical research is completed, divide the project's cost by the number of months required, always dividing by at least one month.
If the monthly cost exceeds the character's gp threshold, the character earns XP equal to the difference per month of research.
procedure.rule: Failing at magical research earns no XP.

distribution_rules.rule: Followers or henchmen conducting magical research earn 50% of the normal magical research XP.
An assistant earns 50% of the magical research XP he would earn if conducting the research independently.
A follower or henchman acting as an assistant therefore earns 25% of normal magical research XP.
Characters do not receive XP for magical research conducted by their assistants.

section.note: The main Strongholds and Domains rules are absent here; only the special cases below remain in force in this document.

establishment.rule: Chaotic adventurers may establish domains of beastmen rather than humans or demi-humans.
The choice is made when the domain is secured.
Instead of clearing beastmen lairs, the adventurer must successfully hire at least one local chieftain as a henchman.
Once the leadership of beastmen lairs in the domain is brought into service, the character becomes a chaotic domain ruler.

exceptions.rule: The ruler may hire any beastmen in the area as mercenaries.
Human and demi-human mercenaries and specialists must be neutral or chaotic.
The ruler attracts beastmen followers and families instead of normal humans.
Beastmen families are of weaker varieties such as kobolds, goblins, or orcs and consist of noncombatants.
Beastmen domains always increase in population as if they were two population categories smaller.
Beastmen provide only 1/2 normal land revenue.
Population limits per hex are reduced to 1/2 normal.
Beastmen in urban settlements produce only 1/2 normal urban revenue.
Domain morale modifiers for garrisons and festivals are doubled.
Lawful rulers only become vassals if conquered and annexed.
Conquered lawful domains suffer a -2 morale penalty due to alignment difference.

subsection.rule: A dwarven vault may only be built in a dwarven realm or wilderness, not in civilized or borderland areas of human or elven realms.
A dwarven vault must be underground.
Above-ground gates, walls, or structures may exist for defense or commerce, but may not exceed 25% of the stronghold's gp value.
Any above-ground structures must be made of earth or stone.
When completed, 3d6 x 10 1st-level dwarven NPCs move in to maintain and defend the vault at no cost.
If additional defenders are needed, the dwarven ruler is expected to employ only dwarven soldiers.
Other races may be hired for non-soldier tasks.
Dwarven vaults are otherwise maintained like human domains.
An elven fastness may only be built in an elven realm or wilderness, not in civilized or borderland areas of human or dwarven realms.
A fastness must be built harmoniously within a site of natural majesty.
Construction cost is equivalent to similar work in stone, even if the fastness is not built of stone.
When completed, 3d6 x 10 1st-level elven NPCs move in to help and defend the fastness at no cost.
If additional defenders are needed, elven spellswords may hire only elven mercenaries.
Non-elves may be hired as specialists and henchmen, but not as mercenaries.
All ordinary animals within 3 miles are friendly to the elves.
The elves may communicate with these animals as per speak with animals.
Animals warn of strangers, carry news, and deliver short messages to nearby places.
Spies and thieves operating against the domain suffer a -2 penalty to proficiency throws.
The elven ruler must defend the animals within this territory.
Elven fastnesses are otherwise maintained like human domains.

general_rules.rule: A 0th-level character may earn XP from campaign activities.
At 100XP from campaign activities, a 0th-level character may advance to 1st level.
0th-level characters are always treated as followers or henchmen and earn 1/2 XP.

path.rule: A 0th-level character studying under an arcane spellcaster of 9th level or higher may become a 1st-level mage.
The character must possess Alchemy, Collegiate Wizardry, Magical Engineering, or a related proficiency at the Judge's discretion.
The character then makes a proficiency throw of 14+, modified by Intelligence bonus or penalty.
path.result: Success advances the character to 1st-level mage.
path.failure: Failure means the character has no gift for magic.

path.rule: A 0th-level character may earn XP from domain and mercantile income.
For this purpose, treat the character's gp threshold as 25gp.
The character advances into a class appropriate to the domain managed.
A 0th-level character may earn XP from hijinks.
Usually the only available hijink is carousing.
Carousing for a 0th-level character uses Hear Noises 18+.
When the character earns 100XP from carousing, he may become a 1st-level assassin, thief, or nightblade.
The final class depends on race and associates.

transition_to_first_level.rule: On advancing to 1st level, the character gains the new class's proficiency, powers, attack throws, and saving throws.
The character rerolls hit points using the new class's hit die and keeps whichever hp total is higher: old or new.
The new 1st-level character keeps any general proficiencies already known.
Upon reaching 2nd, 3rd, and 4th level, the character must remove one of these pre-existing general proficiencies.
At 4th level, the character acquires the Adventuring proficiency.
